title: 2026–2027 Personal Development Plan
position: QA Manager (CRM) — internal CRM / Odoo QA; team of 2 (Anh + 1 QA Engineer)
howToUse: Each row is ONE annual goal read at quarterly checkpoints. This plan starts Q3 2026: 3 months = Oct 2026, 6 = Jan 2027, 9 = Apr 2027, 12 = Jul 2027. TYPE: “Project” = has a finish line, track % to done; “Running” = a continuous standard, read the gauge each checkpoint. [Brackets] = numbers to confirm together at the kickoff 1:1. Status/Comments carries the evidence and history. Context for the whole plan: CRM gets few new features (mostly small improvements) — so the team’s value shifts from feature testing to fast automated post-release checks and performance assurance.

goals.title: Automate the regression base in-team — every release verified by an automated run
checkpoints: Committed Q3 floor: +400 automated TCs (Anh 350 / Thuat 50, via automate_manual_tc_from_jira → Playwright + TypeScript) → ~[31]% of the frozen base; AND the repair debt cleared — the 357 skipped/flaky specs refactored to green (repair adds zero to the count but is priority #1: an untrusted suite cannot gate releases); “automated” definition ratified: the team’s working JQL (Automation scope = Yes + resolved by the automator) raised to a runs-green bar ([3]-stable-pass); regression plan sizes the AUTOMATABLE base — this sets the 12-month bar; full suite producing verdicts on Jenkins on every release build (portal + Allure live since 2026-06-17).

[46]% ≈ [1,710] TCs (+[550] in Q4: Anh [450] + Thuat [100]) — escalation starts once the suite is green, funded by the manual→auto trade: packs now automated stop being executed manually; the pack runs on every release + on a [2-week] schedule (April mid-term goal); skip/flaky rate held <[5]%; maintenance suites (NJM-161297) green.

[63]% ≈ [2,310] (+[600] in Q1-27: Anh [450] + Thuat [150]); post-release verdict < [4] hours; run results feed the all-in-one VP metrics report (NJM-177312 — the Jenkins portal is largely built, close it out); AI-assisted conversion sustained at ≥[4] TC/day, measured.

100% of the automatable base automated & green (bar set by the October sizing; expected ~[70–75]% of all TCs ≈ [2,900] of the frozen 3,693) — the automatable backlog is DONE; every release verified by the automated run BEFORE manual effort starts; manual-only checks reduced to a written exception list; the April long-term goal “automation plan for the whole system” fully delivered and executed.
goals.status: THE core goal — recalibrated after the Q2 QBR + Q3 KPI sheet, then RAISED (Sergii, Jul 2026: better to automate more than run the same TCs manually). Why escalating is realistic: the one-time costs are paid (Jenkins, Allure, conversion tooling) and Q2 itself shows the curve — 52% of the 304 automated TCs took ~9.5 pre-Claude weeks, 48% took the last ~3.5 weeks with Claude ≈ 3× the pace; Q3 stays at the committed 380 only because the 357-spec repair debt eats the surplus. Baseline verified reproducible: his own JQL returns exactly 304 for Q2 (the “created TCs” number is NOT yet reproducible — his sheet says 257, Odoo 330, raw Jira 389 — pin the definition at kickoff). Also bless Anh’s deliberate manual-KPI drop (bugs 60→15, executions 236→120) so the Odoo dashboard isn’t misread. Design fix vs 2025 stands: owned INSIDE the CRM team, AI-assisted, no central-team dependency. Sequencing: new automation targets the post-migration stack (Goal 3) — do not automate the retiring platform twice.

goals.title: Stand up CRM performance testing — from zero to a monthly routine
checkpoints: Quick wins on the EXISTING timing suite: thresholds agreed per action; coverage extended to dashboards / reports / list views — the user-complaint paths the current create/edit timings miss; first monthly trend report published; Create Deal Element ~25s (his own post-fix table) filed as the first perf finding. Env ask unchanged: ONE budget request to the VP in month 1 covering the unstable functional-automation env (Goal 1) AND the perf env with production-like volumes; load tool chosen ([k6 / JMeter / Locust]). CRM-7477 (perf plan, 3 days, Thuat, Q4) proceeds with the env behind it — delegation to Thuat starts at planning, not at month 12.

Load scenarios automated for the top-[10] flows on the perf env; thresholds gate releases that touch critical flows; timing suite runs green under thresholds on every release — at this point the April mid-term goal “performance testing planned and executed” is DONE for real (both layers, not just single-user).

Monthly perf run (timings + load) live with a trend report (April long-term goal); ≥[1] perf regression caught by QA BEFORE any user reports it — the direction-of-causality test this goal exists for (precedents were reactive: NJM-155581, CRM-11415).
Monthly cadence sustained ≥[4] consecutive months; both layers documented & repeatable by Thuat, not only by Anh; zero user-reported perf escapes on covered flows for [2] consecutive quarters.
goals.status: REBASED after CRM-11415 (Jul 2026): Anh already built a single-user perf-baseline capability — the Allure per-build timing view (Create Opp −49%, Edit Contact −74% after dev’s speed bundle) — so the old “from zero” framing was wrong; credit it at the kickoff. What it is NOT yet: load testing (the 2025 Not-done), thresholds, cadence, or early detection — the slowness behind CRM-11415 was reported by USERS while the timings existed, because they do not cover dashboards/reports and nobody watches them against thresholds. CARRIED: 2025 “Run load testing of CRM” (Not done: “missing proper environment”) + April 2026 mid/long-term goals. The env request stays the FIRST checkpoint so the 2025 blocker cannot repeat.

goals.title: Odoo 12 CE → CC migration: business-process regression & sign-off
goals.metric: Planned ONE QUARTER at a time — the migration is too fluid for 12-month commitments (per Sergii, Jul 2026); goals for the next quarter are re-set at each quarterly review from the then-current migration state (cutover date, block list, scope). Standing guardrails that survive every re-plan: every block gets its regression pack BEFORE it ships; integration seams tested, not just modules (the target is a componentized stack: New Build core, GoRules ZEN, Lago subscriptions, OCA exchange rates, Integration Hub ⇄ Zapier & ActiveCampaign); ≤[N] migration escapes post-cutover; packs written automation-ready so they feed Goal 1.
checkpoints: THE committed window (Q3): per-block manual→auto conversion delivered on the published schedule (Jul 23 – Sep 3, ~17 days: Pre-Sale, Discounts, Lead Routing, Subscriptions/Lago, Exchange Rates/OCA, Integration Hub, Customer Support, FTO/Procurement); sandbox test environment as Portal Provider secured (CRM-11138); integration-boundary test packs defined for the seams (Hub ⇄ Zapier/ActiveCampaign, Lago billing, GoRules decisions); migration regression plan with schedule & estimates published (TC inventory in flight: NJM-178587, NJM-176246 done, NJM-178338). At the October review: set the Q4 goals from the then-current migration state.

[Set at the October review.] Candidate items if the migration proceeds on the current path: full migration regression executed; go/no-go verdict + risk list issued by Anh; escape watch running with RCA on anything leaked.
[Set at the January review.] Candidate items: migration TC packs converted into the automated regression (Goal 1) on the new stack; migration escapes ≤[N], all RCA’d.

[Set as the migration confirms — the standing guardrails in the metric column apply regardless.] Direction: migration closed with lessons-learned + coverage map; the new-stack regression base IS the automated base — no duplicate old-system suites left to maintain.
goals.status: Quarter-by-quarter by design: 12-month migration commitments would be fiction (Sergii, Jul 2026) — only the Q3 window is committed; each quarterly review re-plans the next. The big delivery item of H2 2026 — visible in the TC-creation spike (team output 642 TCs in Q1 2026 → 766 in Q2). Escapes will live at the seams (third-party billing, rules engines, Zapier flows): green module tests ≠ a working end-to-end business process.

goals.title: Support stream under control: SLA, trends, and every escape becomes coverage
goals.metric: First response on support tickets ≤[1] business day for ≥[95]% (April long-term goal); quarterly support report published (volumes, categories, trends, time spent); every leaked defect RCA’d on the org unified form with a covering TC in the same [month]; support ≤[20]% of team capacity (time-logged).
checkpoints: Baseline published: 387 CRM support tickets in the last 6 months (Anh 57 / Thuat 253 — delegation is already real); category + time-spent split; SLA measurement switched on; leaked-defect baseline from the Q2 QBR: 4 of 171 valid bugs (~2.3%) — well inside the old <6% target; what remains is the 2025 doubt “I am not confident I know about all of them” — agree the leak-detection rule with the VP so the number is trusted. AI lever launched: Claude + Odoo MCP investigating/resolving support tickets (CRM-11532, from his Q3 AI plan CRM-11531).

First quarterly report delivered (closes the 2025 “Partially done” reporting item); SLA ≥[95]% met; ≥[3] documentation / self-service improvements shipped to cut repeat tickets; AI-assisted share of resolved tickets measured — target [25]% with time-to-resolution trending down.
Escape→RCA→TC loop routine (feeds the org escape-RCA scorecard); repeat-category volume trending down vs baseline.
SLA held all year; support share of team time down [20]% → [15]%, capacity visibly moved to Goals 1–2; zero unknown leaked defects — every one tracked, RCA’d, covered.
goals.status: CARRIED: 2025 “improve support process” = Partially (“too much time spent on it”), support/leak reporting = Partially, 1-business-day SLA = April long-term goal. The load itself is big for a 2-person team (~65 tickets/month) — measurement is what keeps it from silently eating the automation plan.

goals.title: Grow Thuat Phung into an independent second — planning, estimating, owning small improvements
goals.metric: 100% of small improvements planned & estimated by Thuat with Anh as reviewer only; team spec/FRD-review turnaround ≤[2] business days held by the team, not just by Anh; estimates within [±20]%; automation ramp [30–50] (Q3) → [100] (Q4) → [150]/quarter (2027) with his manual-execution goal stepped down in step (660 → [550] → [450]); a 2-week Anh-absence test passed.
checkpoints: Baseline fixed (H1 2026: Thuat 404+436 TCs created, 113+138 valid bugs, 253 support tickets); Thuat plans + estimates his first [2] small improvements end-to-end with Anh reviewing; spec-review SLA measured; automation ramp starts: [30–50] automated TCs in Q3 (30 committed in his KPI sheet — stretch if the ramp goes well), Anh pairing him on the Claude conversion pipeline.

Thuat owns planning/review for ALL small improvements — the April mid-term delegation goal is DONE at this checkpoint; estimates within [±20]%; automation ramp: [100] TCs in Q4, funded by stepping his manual-execution goal down (660 → [550]) as automated packs replace manual regression runs — better to automate than re-run the same TCs by hand (Sergii, Jul 2026).
Anh 2-week absence test: releases checked, support SLA held, nothing waits for him; Thuat at [150] automated TCs/quarter (manual-execution goal down to [450]); KPI trend ≥+[10]% vs baseline.

Thuat sustained at [150] automated TCs/quarter and running small-improvement QA solo — a dual-skill (manual + automation) engineer, not a manual-only IC; Anh’s freed time visibly invested in Goals 1–2 — that reinvestment is the point of delegating.
goals.status: CARRIED from 2025 (“Develop IC so he/she can plan/estimate” — Not done; manager note: “Need to delegate”) and April mid-term. Data says Thuat is ready: output grew every quarter since joining Jun-2025 (TCs 335→341→404→436; valid bugs 39→138/quarter; already carries ~65% of support tickets). Automation ramp RAISED Jul-2026 (Sergii): 30/quarter on an existing framework is a seed, not a pace — target [100–150]/quarter, hours funded by stepping down his manual-execution KPI as automated coverage replaces manual regression. Single-IC team → the absence test is the real bar.
